extracted.intended_audience: authors (and peer reviewers/editors) submitting biomedical research manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on using the EQUATOR Network reporting guidelines (checklists and flow diagrams) to prepare biomedical research manuscripts and comply with journal submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate research reporting guideline for study type
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines provide specific recommendations for the reporting of different types of research. They have been developed to accommodate both general research types (e.g., randomized trials, systematic reviews) and more specific ones (e.g., reporting body fluid biomarker research studies in neurologic disorders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and follow the guideline that matches your study design (examples: CONSORT for randomized trials, STROBE for observational studies, PRISMA for systematic reviews, CARE for case reports, SQUIRE for quality improvement, STARD for diagnostic accuracy, CHEERS for economic evaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include completed guideline checklists and flow diagrams with submission when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasingly, many journals require the inclusion of completed guideline checklists as part of the submission process. Many guidelines include detailed checklists and, in some cases, a flow diagram that displays the progress of all participants through the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide completed checklist(s) and flow diagram(s) as supplemental submission items (typically Word or PDF) when the journal requests them; contact the editorial office to confirm the journal's policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use checklists to confirm essential manuscript elements are present
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist items are not intended to increase the work for authors but to confirm that the essential elements of the manuscript are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the checklist as an author tool to ensure completeness and to help compose and revise the manuscript, not as an additional burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow CARE checklist title requirement for case reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The CARE checklist for the writing of case reports requires that 'The words "case report" should be in the title along with the area of focus'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript title explicitly identifies the article as a case report and indicates the area of focus to comply with CARE items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow STROBE requirement to discuss study limitations, bias, and magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE checklist for the reporting of observational studies outlines that in the Discussion section of your manuscript, the author must 'Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Discussion, explicitly address possible bias sources, imprecision, and describe both the likely direction and magnitude of any bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check journal-specific Instructions for Authors about evidence of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual title may include in the Instructions for Authors specific directions on how to provide evidence of compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submission, review the target journal's Instructions for Authors and, if unclear, contact the editorial office to confirm whether and how to include checklists/flow diagrams and other evidence of reporting-guideline compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EQUATOR Network author toolkit to incorporate guidelines and best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can use the author toolkit on the EQUATOR Network site to understand how to incorporate guidelines and best practice into their writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the EQUATOR author toolkit and other resources on the EQUATOR website for practical tools and explanations on applying reporting guidelines while preparing manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include participant flow diagram for trials where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Some guidelines (for example CONSORT) include a flow diagram that displays the progress of all participants through the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For randomized trials and similar designs, include the recommended participant flow diagram to show enrollment, allocation, follow-up, and analysis numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance signals thoroughness and may speed editorial and peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with these guidelines, as indicated by including the completed checklist (and flow diagram, if applicable) with your submission, provides editorial offices with an indicator of the thoroughness of your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including completed checklists can make reviewers' and editors' work easier by providing a consistent submission structure, which could help speed the editorial decision process and present the work as high-quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines are expert-developed and credible
rubrics_metrics.description: They are written by experts in study design, epidemiology, biostatistics, and research methodology, and have been developed to accommodate both general and specific research types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on these expert-developed guidelines as authoritative sources for what information should be reported; where specialized guidelines exist for narrow topics, prefer them over generic guidance.
